topics.description: A French military helmet designed by Louis Adrian in 1915, distinguished by a raised ridge along its crown.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of these objects designed in 1915 by Louis Adrian [loo-ee ay-dree-un] had a distinct ridge at the top and was adopted by the French Army. Another of them designed by John Leopold Brodie was nicknamed the “doughboy” by American soldiers. Frederick William IV designed one of these objects made of boiled leather, called the Pickelhaube [pickle-how-buh], which had a (*) distinctive upward spike. In 1916 Germany introduced a steel type of these objects whose “coal scuttle” shape was widely used in propaganda. This worn piece of equipment protected soldiers from falling shrapnel during World War I. For 10 points, name this piece of armor worn on the head.
parts.answer: World War I helmets [accept Adrian helmets or Brodie helmets or Stahlhelme]

topics.description: A Bronze Age civilization centered in mainland Greece that used Linear B and is associated with the society depicted in Homeric war poems.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Bronze Age Collapse was a sudden disruption for many major ancient civilizations. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: The collapse affected civilizations around the eastern side of this body of water. Before the collapse, traders would sail on it from the Nile Delta in Egypt to the Hittite Empire in Anatolia.
parts.answer: Mediterranean Sea

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Dorian invasion of Greece during the Bronze Age Collapse spelled the end of this proto-Greek civilization. This culture wrote in Linear B script and is thought to be the civilization depicted in Homer’s war poems.
parts.answer: Mycenean Greeks

parts.label: C
parts.question: Mycenaeans (my-SEE-nee-anz) heavily practiced this art form, creating many vases and urns. Through this art form, they would display floral designs or depict the events of their myths.
parts.answer: pottery

topics.description: A 1497 Florentine public burning of objects considered sinful, associated with the Dominican preacher Girolamo Savonarola.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A powerful family that ruled this city included men like Lorezno the Magnificent. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Italian city once ruled by the Medici family. This city is the most populous one in Tuscany.
parts.answer: Florence [or Firenze]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In 1378, Florence was the site of the Ciompi Revolt, initiated by disgruntled producers of this textile good, which comes from sheep.
parts.answer: wool

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] While de facto ruler of Florence, Girolama Savonarola ordered one of these specific events to purge the city of sinful items like books, paintings, and musical instruments.
parts.answer: Bonfire of the Vanities [prompt on Bonfire]

topics.description: The ABC Powers were Argentina, Brazil, and Chile, which mediated negotiations between the United States and Mexico in 1914.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The “ABC Powers” mediated a conference between American and Mexican diplomats in 1914. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: The “ABC Powers” are Argentina, Brazil, and this South American country whose capital is Santiago.
parts.answer: Chile (accept Republic of Chile; accept Republica de ´ Chile)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Among the relatively few conflicts between the ABC powers is a border dispute between Chile and Argentina over this cold region of South America south of the Pampas.
parts.answer: Patagonia

parts.label: C
parts.question: Before they were the “ABC Powers”, Argentina and Brazil joined with Uruguay in the 19th century War of the Triple Alliance against this country, which lost the war decisively.
parts.answer: Paraguay (accept Republic of Paraguay; accept Republica del ´ Paraguay; accept Tavakuaireta Paraguai´ )

topics.description: A January 2015 Islamist terrorist attack in France that targeted the satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo over its cartoons of Muhammad.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A deputy chief of staff for this country's president impersonated a police officer and beat a  protester in 2018 in what became known as the Benalla (beh-NAH-lah) affair. Teacher Samuel Paty  (sam-yoo-EL paa-TEE) was beheaded after a false accusation in this country, five years after this  country's Hypercacher (ee-PAIR-kaa-SHAY) market and (*) satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo (SHAH-lee eb-doh) were attacked over cartoons depicting Muhammad. This country's 2022 presidential  election ended in the run-off defeat of far-right candidate Marine Le Pen (mah-RIN lay pen). For 10  points, name this country led by president Emmanuel Macron.
parts.answer: France [or French Republic; or République française]

topics.description: Operation Opera was Israel's 1981 airstrike that destroyed Iraq's Osirak nuclear reactor near Baghdad.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This ruler wrote a novel titled Begone, Demons, that features an allusion to the 9/11 attacks. Israel launched Operation Opera to destroy the Osirak nuclear reactor this ruler had bought from France. Apocryphally, this ruler commissioned a copy of the Quran written in his own blood. This ruler was captured while hiding in a “spider hole” during Operation Red Dawn. This ruler’s first cousin was nicknamed (*) “Chemical” Ali for his use of chemical weapons during the al-Anfal campaign against Kurds. This ruler’s forces used the “Highway of Death” to retreat from a 1990 invasion of Kuwait. For 10 points, name this dictator of Iraq who was overthrown after the 2003 US invasion.
parts.answer: Saddam Hussein [or Saddam Hussein Abd al-Majid al-Tikriti; accept Saddam]

topics.description: The late-19th-century Argentine military campaign that expanded state control over Patagonia and displaced or killed many Indigenous peoples, including the Mapuche.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country's politics were once dominated by the “Generation of '80,” including Julio Roca,  who earlier displaced the Mapuche (mah-POO-chay) people during this country's Conquest of the  Desert. The 25th article of this country's 1853 constitution promoted European immigration,  leading to 60% of this country's present-day population having (*) Italian ancestry. The 1881  Boundary Treaty divided Tierra del Fuego (tee-AIR-ah del FWAY-goh) between this country and a  smaller neighbor that shares Patagonia. For 10 points, name this country that has a 3300-mile long  border with Chile.
parts.answer: Argentina [or Argentine Republic; or Republica Argentina]

topics.description: A defensive structure, often built from stone or brick, used to protect settlements and territories from attack.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this series, the Scout Regiment maneuvers with ODM gear to strike the napes of the beings that partially title this series. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this manga series, whose protagonist is Eren Jaeger. In this series, humanity is pushed to the brink of extinction by the large humanoid steam-emitting beings that partially title this series.
parts.answer: Attack on Titan [or AOT or Shingeki no Kyojin]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The remaining humans live behind Maria, Rose, and Sina, concentric examples of these large defensive structures, typically made out of stones or bricks.
parts.answer: wall

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The appearance of the largest and most recognizable titan, the Colossal, completely lacks this feature, which is removed in the process of flaying.
parts.answer: skin [or skinned or skinless]

topics.description: The formal writing system of ancient Egypt that combines logographic, consonantal, and determinative signs and was deciphered in the modern era through the Rosetta Stone.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Thomas Young aided in Jean-François Champollion’s (sham-POL-ee-on) analysis of this object, which was rediscovered during a Napoleonic campaign. This object celebrates the anniversary of Ptolemy (TAH-luh-mee) V’s coronation in three scripts, including (*) Ancient Greek and Demotic. For ten points, name this rock which was used to interpret Egyptian hieroglyphics, which a brand of language-learning software is named after.
parts.answer: Rosetta Stone

topics.description: Filipino president and authoritarian ruler who was overthrown by the 1986 People Power Revolution amid accusations surrounding the assassination of Benigno “Ninoy” Aquino Jr.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about yellow ribbons in history, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Hundreds of yellow ribbons were used in demonstrations in the People Power Revolution, which removed this leader. This man was accused of having senator Ninoy Aquino assassinated.
parts.answer: Ferdinand Marcos [or Ferdinand Emmanuel Edralin Marcos Sr.]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Canada launched Operation Yellow Ribbon in response to this event, which inspired the musical Come From Away. The town of Gander in Newfoundland housed many people stranded in this event.
parts.answer: 9/11 [or September 11th attacks]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Victims of the Sewol ferry disaster in this country are commemorated with yellow ribbons. The Miracle on the Han River refers to massive growth in this country’s capital of Seoul.
parts.answer: South Korea [or the Republic of Korea; or ROK; prompt on Korea; reject “North Korea” or the “Democratic People’s Republic of Korea”]
